title: Whole Grain Pasta with Cream Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with cream sauce is a restaurant‑style dish made from whole‑grain pasta, which retains the nutty flavor and nutrients of the grain, paired with a smooth cream sauce prepared from cream, butter, and aromatic herbs. The pasta provides a hearty texture while the sauce adds a luxurious, velvety finish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains more fiber and micronutrients than refined white pasta.
The cream sauce is often enriched with Parmesan, garlic, and fresh herbs to deepen its flavor.
Restaurants frequently garnish the dish with toasted pumpkin or sunflower seeds for added crunch.
The combination of whole grain pasta and cream sauce originated in Italy in the early 20th century as chefs experimented with more nutritious alternatives.
Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index, helping to moderate blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates deliver steady energy without rapid glucose spikes.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The pasta supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Healthy fats in the sauce
items.content: Cream‑based sauce contributes monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that can support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cream provides calcium, and fortified cream can add vitamin D, both important for bone health.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The cream sauce adds significant calories; portion control is advisable, especially for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream and butter contain lactose; those with intolerance should use lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the dairy components of the sauce.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: When cheese and salt are added, the dish can become high in sodium, which may be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossed with the cream sauce. Add sautéed vegetables, grilled chicken, or seafood for extra protein. Finish with grated Parmesan, fresh herbs, and a pinch of black pepper.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry whole grain pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked pasta with sauce should be kept in the refrigerator in a sealed container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of cream to restore the sauce’s silky texture.
